narrative:
We have a sunny, seasonal Sunday and Monday. The only item of note is a dry front moving across the region from the northwest later tonight. Windy conditions develop and last well into Monday. Temperatures are a couple of degrees cooler Monday. Tuesday and Wednesday are slightly warmer. Forecast Discussion

High pressure over the Tennessee Valley brings a sunny, seasonal Sunday. A dry front crosses from the northwest late tonight with no rain, but the wind picks up after midnight and stays gusty well into Monday.

High pressure moves off the Carolina coast Tuesday and Wednesday, and afternoons turn slightly warmer. Valleys stay frosty at night.

A cold front crosses the mountains Thursday. Showers develop early Thursday, especially on the west side of the Appalachians. Rain showers change to snow showers from west to east around midnight as much colder air arrives.

Snow showers continue Friday and Friday night on a cold, windy northwest flow. Accumulations are greatest at higher elevations and along the western edge of the Appalachians, with flurries reaching the Blue Ridge (east). Snow showers taper to flurries Saturday. Prepare for a cold, windy, wintry weekend.
